sentences.en: Starbucks workers at the Elmwood Avenue location voted to unionize.
sentences.zh: 位于埃尔姆伍德大道的星巴克员工投票决定成立工会。

sentences.en: Final tally, 19 to 8.
sentences.zh: 最终票数，19比8。

sentences.en: It's significant because that is the first Starbucks to form a union at a company-operated store ever in America.
sentences.zh: 这意义重大，因为这是美国有史以来第一家由公司直营并成立工会的星巴克门店。

sentences.en: Unionization efforts have been gaining steam across major companies.
sentences.zh: 各大公司的工会化努力正日益升温。

sentences.en: Today, Amazon workers at a Staten Island warehouse successfully voted to unionize.
sentences.zh: 今天，亚马逊斯塔滕岛仓库的员工投票成功成立了工会。

sentences.en: Workers at the New York City location of outdoor clothing and equipment seller REI have voted in favor of joining a union.
sentences.zh: 户外服装和装备零售商 REI 纽约市门店的员工也投票赞成加入工会。

sentences.en: Now, this is the first major effort at an Apple store.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是苹果门店首次出现重大的工会化努力。

sentences.en: Because they made this all popular.
sentences.zh: 因为他们让这一切变得流行起来。

sentences.en: We went for the juggler and we went for the top dog because we want every other industry, every other business to know that things have changed.
sentences.zh: 我们直击要害，瞄准了行业巨头，因为我们想让其他所有行业、所有企业都知道，情况已经变了。

sentences.en: We're going to unionize.
sentences.zh: 我们要成立工会。

sentences.en: We're not going to quit our jobs anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不会轻易辞职了。

sentences.en: My colleague, Noam Scheiber, on the largest gain in union membership in U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的同事诺姆·谢伯将讲述美国历史上工会会员人数增长最快的时期——20世纪30年代，以及那个时代对当下的启示。

sentences.en: history, the 1930s, and what that era tells us about today.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月2日，星期一。

sentences.en: It's Monday,
sentences.zh: 今天是星期一，

sentences.en: May 2nd.
sentences.zh: 5月2日。

sentences.en: So, Noam, you cover labor for The New York Times, and I've been hearing a lot of reports about this flurry of activity with unions.
sentences.zh: 诺姆，你负责《纽约时报》的劳工报道，我最近听到很多关于工会活动激增的报道。

sentences.en: We did an episode last month about this organizing in an Amazon warehouse in New York, and there are other reports too.
sentences.zh: 上个月我们做了一期关于纽约亚马逊仓库组织工会的节目，还有其他类似的报道。

sentences.en: So, I wanted to ask you, what are you seeing in terms of actual numbers?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想问你，从实际数据来看，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, we are definitely seeing signs of a revival in union membership.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实看到了工会会员人数复苏的迹象。

sentences.en: You know, before you form a union, at least one that's certified by the federal government,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在成立工会之前，至少是联邦政府认证的工会，

sentences.en: you have to file a petition for an election with an agency called the National Labor Relations
sentences.zh: 你必须向一个名为国家劳资关系委员会的机构提交选举申请。

sentences.en: Board.
sentences.zh: 委员会。

sentences.en: And once you file that petition, then you and your co-workers can vote and vote in a union potentially that the government will effectively bless.
sentences.zh: 一旦提交了申请，你和你的同事就可以投票，并可能成立一个政府会予以认可的工会。

sentences.en: And what we've seen is that over the past six months, those filings are up 60 percent over the same period one year earlier.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，在过去六个月里，这些申请数量比去年同期增长了60%。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: 60 percent.
So, a big surge in intent to form a union.
sentences.zh: 所以，成立工会的意愿出现了大幅激增。

sentences.en: Yes, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常明显。

sentences.en: In my seven years covering unions for The Times, I've never seen a jump that big.
sentences.zh: 在我为《时报》报道工会工作的七年里，我从未见过如此大的涨幅。

sentences.en: And it really is actually at odds with the trend, both in my lifetime and my career covering this stuff.
sentences.zh: 这实际上与我这一生以及我从事相关报道以来的趋势背道而驰。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, my understanding of the story of unions is that it's been one of decline.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对工会历史的理解是，它一直处于衰落之中。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We're down from about a third of American workers in a union at its peak to about 10 percent today.
sentences.zh: 我们已经从巅峰时期约占美国劳动者三分之一的工会比例，下降到今天的约10%。

sentences.en: So, it's quite dramatic.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常戏剧性。

sentences.en: And it turns out that unions are a really, really big deal for workers.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，工会对劳动者来说确实非常重要。

sentences.en: There's a pretty big body of research showing that workers in unions make significantly more money than workers of the same profile who are not in unions.
sentences.zh: 有大量研究表明，工会成员的收入明显高于同等条件下的非工会成员。

sentences.en: And over time, what we've seen is that as unions have declined, wages for a lot of workers, even workers not in unions, have tended to stagnate.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们看到随着工会的衰落，许多劳动者的工资，即使是非工会成员，也往往陷入停滞。

sentences.en: We've seen a real rise in income inequality, a real concentration of wealth at the top.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了收入不平等的加剧，财富在顶层高度集中。

sentences.en: And all of this has corresponded to this really tough era for unions.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都与工会经历的这段艰难时期相对应。

sentences.en: And so, a lot of people think that if you could trigger some sort of revival of the labor movement, you would start to
sentences.zh: 因此，很多人认为，如果你能引发某种劳工运动的复兴，你就会开始

sentences.en: see a reversal of all these trends that we've sort of bemoaned over the past several decades.
sentences.zh: 看到过去几十年来我们一直感叹的所有趋势出现逆转。

sentences.en: And so, it could really, really be a big deal for workers and for the economy and for the entire country.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对劳动者、经济乃至整个国家来说，都可能是一件大事。

sentences.en: So, Noam, do we know if the rise in filings you're talking about will actually result in reversing that decline, that decline in union membership?
sentences.zh: 诺姆，我们是否知道你所说的申请数量增加，是否真的会导致工会会员人数下降趋势的逆转？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: But what we do know is that historically, a lot of things have to align at the same time for union membership to really take off.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道的是，从历史上看，工会会员人数要真正实现增长，很多因素必须同时具备。

sentences.en: It's not just that the working conditions are bad.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为工作条件恶劣。

sentences.en: It's not just that workers are feeling emboldened or that inequality is really high.
sentences.zh: 也不仅仅是因为劳动者感到受鼓舞，或者不平等现象非常严重。

sentences.en: It's that all these things kind of happen at the same time.
sentences.zh: 而是所有这些事情在同一时间发生了。

sentences.en: But the good news for unions is that if these things do align, the growth in union membership can be really, really quick.
sentences.zh: 但对工会来说好消息是，如果这些因素确实汇聚在一起，工会会员人数的增长可能会非常非常快。

sentences.en: And we actually saw this play out in the 1930s when we saw a huge expansion of union membership in a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上在20世纪30年代就看到了这种情况，当时工会会员人数在很短的时间内出现了巨大的扩张。

sentences.en: What exactly was happening in that period to prompt that huge expansion of unions?
sentences.zh: 那个时期究竟发生了什么，促成了工会如此巨大的扩张？

sentences.en: In the 1920s, the great American word was prosperity.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪20年代，美国最伟大的词汇是“繁荣”。

sentences.en: Now the 30s have begun and there is a new word,
sentences.zh: 现在30年代开始了，出现了一个新词，

sentences.en: depression.
sentences.zh: “萧条”。

sentences.en: The country was in the throes of the Great Depression, which had obviously been an incredibly traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 国家正处于大萧条的阵痛中，这显然是一场极其痛苦的事件。

sentences.en: Little man, what now?
sentences.zh: 小人物，现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: Well, you can always sell surplus apples, five cents apiece on the street corner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你总能在街角卖掉多余的苹果，每个五美分。

sentences.en: And if you're bewildered, panicky at what's happening to you in your country, you aren't alone.
sentences.zh: 如果你对发生在你和国家身上的事情感到困惑和恐慌，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: But then things started to shift.
sentences.zh: 但随后情况开始转变。

sentences.en: Our responsibility is to all of the people in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们的责任是为这个国家的所有人民服务。

sentences.en: This is a great national crusade, a crusade to destroy enforced idleness, which is an enemy of the human spirit generated by this depression.
sentences.zh: 这是一场伟大的全国性运动，一场旨在消除强制性闲置的运动，这是大萧条产生的人类精神之敌。

sentences.en: At the same time, you started to have Congress pass and President Franklin Roosevelt signed laws that actually made it easier for workers to organize a union.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，国会开始通过法律，富兰克林·罗斯福总统签署了这些法律，实际上让劳动者更容易组织工会。

sentences.en: To enforce minimum wages, to prevent excessive hours, to safeguard, define and enforce collective bargaining.
sentences.zh: 强制执行最低工资，防止过度加班，保障、定义并执行集体谈判。

sentences.en: For the first time, it created a federally protected right to unionize.
sentences.zh: 这是第一次创造了联邦保护的工会化权利。

sentences.en: You couldn't be fired for trying to unionize.
sentences.zh: 你不能因为试图成立工会而被解雇。

sentences.en: There was a process for voting in a union.
sentences.zh: 有了一套成立工会的投票程序。

sentences.en: These things hadn't existed before, but FDR creates that essentially in the mid-1930s.
sentences.zh: 这些在以前并不存在，但罗斯福总统在20世纪30年代中期基本上创造了这些。

sentences.en: And then the economy is actually starting to improve a bit.
sentences.zh: 然后经济实际上开始有所好转。

sentences.en: Unemployment is still very high, but it appears to be moving in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 失业率仍然很高，但似乎正朝着正确的方向发展。

sentences.en: Never since my inauguration in March 1933 have I felt so unmistakably the atmosphere of American recovery.
sentences.zh: 自1933年3月就职以来，我从未如此清晰地感受到美国复苏的气息。

sentences.en: Workers are feeling a little bit better about their prospects.
sentences.zh: 劳动者对他们的前景感觉好了一些。

sentences.en: Companies are starting to do better.
sentences.zh: 公司开始好转。

sentences.en: Sales are increasing.
sentences.zh: 销售额在增加。

sentences.en: Profits are coming back.
sentences.zh: 利润正在回归。

sentences.en: And especially at some very large manufacturing companies like General Motors, you really start to see a rebound.
sentences.zh: 特别是在通用汽车这样的大型制造公司，你真的开始看到反弹。

sentences.en: Chevrolet Motor Company will announce a great new car.
sentences.zh: 雪佛兰汽车公司将宣布一款伟大的新车。

sentences.en: If you think back to the 1930s, GM was really at the forefront of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想20世纪30年代，通用汽车确实处于美国经济的前沿。

sentences.en: economy.
sentences.zh: 经济。

sentences.en: The auto industry in those days was almost like the tech industry today.
sentences.zh: 当时的汽车工业几乎就像今天的科技行业。

sentences.en: It was seen as this rising power.
sentences.zh: 它被视为一股正在崛起的力量。

sentences.en: You will get the thrill of a smooth 60-horsepower six-cylinder engine with a speed of 65 to 70 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 你将体验到平稳的60马力六缸发动机带来的快感，时速可达65到70英里。

sentences.en: Cars had been around for a little while, but they were still relatively new technologies,
sentences.zh: 汽车已经出现了一段时间，但它们仍然是相对较新的技术，

sentences.en: and they were seen as this thing that was going to kind of drive growth and take us into the future.
sentences.zh: 它们被视为一种将推动增长并引领我们走向未来的事物。

sentences.en: You will get the thrill of ultramodern styling in smart new bodies by Fisher.
sentences.zh: 你将获得费舍尔公司打造的智能新车身所带来的超现代造型的快感。

sentences.en: We believe it is unquestionably the finest motor car this company has ever designed or built.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，这无疑是本公司设计或制造的最精美的汽车。

sentences.en: So it was the central piece of the American economy that was also new, and it was really starting to see sales increase at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以它是美国经济的核心部分，而且也是新的，当时销售额确实开始增长。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: GM and the other automakers were really starting to bounce back.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车和其他汽车制造商确实开始反弹。

sentences.en: At the time, in the mid-1930s, GM employed about 250,000 workers, and they were producing about half the vehicles in the country.
sentences.zh: 当时，在20世纪30年代中期，通用汽车雇佣了约25万名工人，生产了全国约一半的汽车。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But there were some issues for workers that made it complicated, at the very leaSt. The first one is
sentences.zh: 但对工人来说，有一些问题让情况变得复杂，至少是这样。第一个问题是

sentences.en: GM would typically shut its factories down once or twice a year, and workers could be out of work
sentences.zh: 通用汽车通常每年会关闭工厂一到两次，工人们可能会失业

sentences.en: for a month or two months while this retooling happened, and that was leading to some real anxiety and frustration.
sentences.zh: 一到两个月，因为工厂要进行设备改造，这导致了一些真正的焦虑和挫败感。

sentences.en: There's just a sense of, at any moment, you could be unemployed, and no one wanted to be unemployed after the trauma of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种感觉，随时都可能失业，在大萧条的创伤之后，没有人想失业。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The second thing that really was starting to build frustration in these factories was something that workers referred to with this kind of catch-all term called the speed-up.
sentences.zh: 第二件让工厂里的挫败感开始积累的事情，是工人们用一个统称来形容的词，叫“加速”。

sentences.en: And the speed-up was this general idea that GM and the factories were going to continue to push you faster and faster and faster until your body was basically used up.
sentences.zh: “加速”是一个普遍的概念，即通用汽车和工厂会不断地催促你，越来越快，直到你的身体基本上被耗尽。

sentences.en: Workers talked about having foremen just kind of looming over them with stopwatches.
sentences.zh: 工人们谈到工头拿着秒表在他们头上盘旋。

sentences.en: And workers would talk about having to make like 100, 110, 120 hand motions per minute.
sentences.zh: 工人们会谈到每分钟必须完成100、110、120个手部动作。

sentences.en: So this was just an incredibly grueling job.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一份极其艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: And as time went on, people found that their bodies were really just breaking down.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，人们发现他们的身体真的在崩溃。

sentences.en: Okay, so it sounds like these jobs were hard physically, but they were also hard psychologically because they were unpredictable.
sentences.zh: 好吧，听起来这些工作不仅体力上很累，心理上也因为不可预测而变得艰难。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on top of that, there was a final factor, which is workers knew that the company was starting to do well again.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，还有一个最终因素，那就是工人们知道公司开始好转了。

sentences.en: And in fact, some of the most visible figures running the company, not least Alfred Sloan, who was the longtime president and chief executive of GM,
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些经营公司的最显眼的人物，尤其是通用汽车长期担任总裁兼首席执行官的阿尔弗雷德·斯隆，

sentences.en: were incredibly wealthy, powerful figures.
sentences.zh: 都是极其富有和有权势的人物。

sentences.en: Alfred Sloan at the time was almost like a Jeff Bezos or an Elon Musk character today.
sentences.zh: 当时的阿尔弗雷德·斯隆几乎就像今天的杰夫·贝佐斯或埃隆·马斯克。

sentences.en: He boasted about being worth $70 million, which in today's dollars would be well over a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 他吹嘘自己拥有7000万美元的财富，按今天的美元计算，这远超十亿美元。

sentences.en: And workers just couldn't sort of fathom why, if the company was doing so well and producing such wealthy executives, why their lives couldn't be made a little bit easier.
sentences.zh: 工人们无法理解，如果公司经营得这么好，产生了如此富有的高管，为什么他们的生活不能变得轻松一点。

sentences.en: So in terms of the conditions you were talking about that have to line up, it sounds like what
sentences.zh: 所以，就你所说的必须具备的条件而言，听起来我们在这里看到的是，

sentences.en: we're seeing here is, you know, this federal support for unions, workers experiencing pretty terrible working conditions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，联邦政府对工会的支持，工人们经历着非常糟糕的工作条件。

sentences.en: And at the same time, GM is actually doing incredibly well.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，通用汽车实际上表现得非常好。

sentences.en: The economy is on the rebound.
sentences.zh: 经济正在反弹。

sentences.en: It's selling tons of cars.
sentences.zh: 它卖出了大量的汽车。

sentences.en: And workers are seeing that.
sentences.zh: 工人们看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And they're saying, hey, why don't we get more out of this?
sentences.zh: 他们说，嘿，为什么我们不能从中得到更多？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think there was one additional factor that may be underappreciated, but was actually really
sentences.zh: 我认为还有一个可能被低估但实际上非常重要的因素，

sentences.en: important, which is that even though these workers were toiling away in pretty lousy conditions, they were not the lowest rung workers in the workforce.
sentences.zh: 那就是尽管这些工人在相当糟糕的条件下劳作，但他们并不是劳动力中最低层的人。

sentences.en: A lot of them had some skills.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人拥有一些技能。

sentences.en: Some of them were even quite educated.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至受过相当好的教育。

sentences.en: They saw themselves as being powerful, not powerless.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己是有力量的，而不是无力的。

sentences.en: And, you know, they actually made typically more than the average worker.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们通常比普通工人挣得多。

sentences.en: All of this kind of gave them a sense that when things were not great at work, they might be able to change it.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都让他们觉得，当工作不顺心时，他们或许能够改变它。

sentences.en: They might be able to take matters into their own hands.
sentences.zh: 他们或许能够把命运掌握在自己手中。

sentences.en: So what do these workers do?
sentences.zh: 那么这些工人做了什么？

sentences.en: So they actually start a union.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上成立了一个工会。

sentences.en: The United Automobile Workers Union is founded in 1935.
sentences.zh: 全美汽车工人联合会成立于1935年。

sentences.en: And at first, it's a pretty weak union.
sentences.zh: 起初，这是一个相当弱小的工会。

sentences.en: But by 1936, something starts to happen.
sentences.zh: 但到了1936年，事情开始发生变化。

sentences.en: In July of that year, there's a terrible heat wave in the MidweSt. It's over 100 degrees for about a week.
sentences.zh: 那年7月，中西部地区出现了可怕的热浪，气温连续一周超过100华氏度。

sentences.en: And workers in these factories are really feeling it.
sentences.zh: 这些工厂里的工人们真的感受到了。

sentences.en: They're getting heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 他们正在中暑。

sentences.en: They're going to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他们正被送往医院。

sentences.en: Some are dying.
sentences.zh: 有些人快不行了。

sentences.en: And so the union starts to gain momentum.
sentences.zh: 工会因此开始积蓄力量。

sentences.en: And it's signing more and more people up.
sentences.zh: 加入的人越来越多。

sentences.en: But they're not really successful at getting the company to recognize them.
sentences.zh: 但他们没能成功让公司承认工会地位。

sentences.en: And the leaders of the UAW decide that they have to do something really dramatic in order to get GM's attention.
sentences.zh: 全美汽车工人联合会（UAW）的领导层决定，必须采取一些非常激进的行动来引起通用汽车的注意。

sentences.en: These were days when history changed its course.
sentences.zh: 那是一个历史转折的时代。

sentences.en: The sit-down strikes began on December 30th.
sentences.zh: 静坐罢工始于12月30日。

sentences.en: And so on December 30th of 1936, at seven in the morning at a plant in Flint, 50 workers sit down at their workstations.
sentences.zh: 1936年12月30日早上七点，在弗林特的一家工厂里，50名工人坐在工作岗位上拒绝离开。

sentences.en: And the decision to sit down is actually a strategic one.
sentences.zh: 静坐的决定其实是一种策略。

sentences.en: Because if you sit down at your workstation, and the company wants to disrupt the strike, they have to come in and
sentences.zh: 因为如果你坐在工作岗位上，而公司想要破坏罢工，他们就必须进来并

sentences.en: physically remove you, which is much harder than if you're outside striking, and they just send in other workers.
sentences.zh: 强行把你赶走，这比你在外面罢工、公司直接换一批工人进来要困难得多。

sentences.en: And so this sit-down starts at that plant in Flint.
sentences.zh: 于是，这场静坐罢工就在弗林特的那家工厂开始了。

sentences.en: By the end of that day, it spreads to a much bigger plant in Flint.
sentences.zh: 到当天结束时，罢工蔓延到了弗林特规模更大的工厂。

sentences.en: And over the next few days, it's spreading all across the
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几天里，罢工蔓延到了整个

sentences.en: MidweSt. Workers also establish picket lines in Cleveland, Ohio, Norwood, Ohio, Toledo, Ohio,
sentences.zh: 中西部地区。工人们还在俄亥俄州的克利夫兰、诺伍德、托莱多，

sentences.en: Janesville, Wisconsin, St. Louis, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州的简斯维尔，以及密苏里州的圣路易斯建立了纠察线。

sentences.en: This thing has really become a bona fide strike.
sentences.zh: 这已经演变成了一场名副其实的罢工。

sentences.en: Roughly half of GM's workforce of 250,000 people are pretty quickly striking at their plants.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车25万名员工中，约有一半人很快就在各自的工厂参与了罢工。

sentences.en: The few hundred workers who had the leading roles in the strike stayed in the plant.
sentences.zh: 在罢工中起带头作用的几百名工人留在了工厂内部。

sentences.en: Thousands on the outside carried on their important parts.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的工人在外面发挥着重要的支持作用。

sentences.en: While the sit-in strikers maintained a disciplined existence inside the plants and sang, when they tie a can to a union man, sit down, sit down.
sentences.zh: 当静坐罢工者在工厂内保持纪律并歌唱时，他们唱道：当他们把罐头系在工会成员身上时，坐下，坐下。

sentences.en: When they give him the sack, they'll take him back.
sentences.zh: 当他们解雇他时，他们会把他请回来。

sentences.en: Sit down, sit down.
sentences.zh: 坐下，坐下。

sentences.en: When the speed up comes, just twiddle your thumbs.
sentences.zh: 当工作节奏加快时，就转动你的大拇指。

sentences.en: Sit down, sit down.
sentences.zh: 坐下，坐下。

sentences.en: When the boss won't talk, don't take a walk.
sentences.zh: 当老板不愿谈话时，别走开。

sentences.en: Sit down, sit down.
sentences.zh: 坐下，坐下。

sentences.en: They sang, and they dug in for the duration.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着歌，做好了长期抗争的准备。

sentences.en: GM is really starting to feel this.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车真的开始感受到压力了。

sentences.en: They're losing millions of dollars each week.
sentences.zh: 他们每周损失数百万美元。

sentences.en: And so on January
sentences.zh: 于是到了1月

sentences.en: 11th, about two weeks in, they decide to respond.
sentences.zh: 11日，也就是罢工两周后，他们决定反击。

sentences.en: And what they do is two things.
sentences.zh: 他们采取了两项措施。

sentences.en: They cut off the heat at this big plant in Flint, and it's only 16 degrees outside.
sentences.zh: 他们切断了弗林特这家大工厂的供暖，而外面只有16华氏度（约零下9摄氏度）。

sentences.en: So pretty quickly, it's very chilly inside the plant.
sentences.zh: 所以很快，工厂内部就变得非常寒冷。

sentences.en: And two, when supporters of the strikers come in to bring food that evening, company police officer, company security person blocks the shipment of food.
sentences.zh: 第二，当那天晚上罢工者的支持者送食物进来时，公司警卫、公司安保人员阻拦了食物的运送。

sentences.en: food.
sentences.zh: 食物。

sentences.en: And suddenly, all hell breaks loose.
sentences.zh: 突然间，一切都乱套了。

sentences.en: What observers describe as the most crucial battle in
sentences.zh: 观察家们将其描述为美国劳工史上最关键的一场战役，

sentences.en: American labor history, involving nearly 100,000 men, has practically shut down the entire American motor industry.
sentences.zh: 涉及近10万名工人，几乎瘫痪了整个美国汽车工业。

sentences.en: From Michigan, where the strike started, we bring you these actual pictures of a riot in progress.
sentences.zh: 从罢工开始的密歇根州，我们为您带来这些正在发生的骚乱的真实画面。

sentences.en: There's a complete melee that goes on.
sentences.zh: 现场陷入了一片混乱。

sentences.en: What happens when a crowd of strikers grows crazy when destruction becomes the order of the day?
sentences.zh: 当一群罢工者变得疯狂，当破坏成为当天的常态时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Flint police arrive.
sentences.zh: 弗林特警方赶到了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, workers are defending their positions.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，工人们正在捍卫自己的阵地。

sentences.en: They're throwing bottles and rocks and equipment.
sentences.zh: 他们投掷瓶子、石块和设备。

sentences.en: Local police use tear gas in a last effort to disperse the crowd.
sentences.zh: 当地警察在最后关头使用催泪瓦斯试图驱散人群。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, the police use tear gas to try to subdue the workers.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，警察使用催泪瓦斯试图制服工人。

sentences.en: But luckily for the workers, the wind blows the tear gas back at the policemen.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，风把催泪瓦斯吹回到了警察身上。

sentences.en: This is not vandalism you see there.
sentences.zh: 你看到的这些不是蓄意破坏。

sentences.en: They are breaking these windows to let the air in and to let the tear gas out.
sentences.zh: 他们打破窗户是为了通风，让催泪瓦斯散去。

sentences.en: And eventually, this is known as the Battle of the Running Bulls.
sentences.zh: 最终，这场冲突被称为“奔跑的公牛之战”。

sentences.en: Bulls being slain for police because they were actually forced to retreat by the use of their own tear gas, which got in their eyes and caused them to disperse.
sentences.zh: “公牛”是警察的蔑称，因为他们实际上被自己使用的催泪瓦斯逼退了，瓦斯进入了他们的眼睛，导致他们四散奔逃。

sentences.en: And a lot of these details come from a University of
sentences.zh: 这些细节大多来自密歇根大学

sentences.en: Michigan historian named Sidney Fine, who wrote a definitive account of this strike.
sentences.zh: 的历史学家西德尼·法恩，他撰写了关于这场罢工的权威记录。

sentences.en: And what Fine describes is that next, the governor of Michigan, who is an ally of President Roosevelt, a progressive governor, sends in the National Guard.
sentences.zh: 法恩描述说，接下来，密歇根州州长——他是罗斯福总统的盟友，一位进步派州长——派出了国民警卫队。

sentences.en: But critically, he tells them, you're just there to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 但关键是，他告诉他们，你们去那里只是为了维持和平。

sentences.en: You're not supposed to crush the strike.
sentences.zh: 你们不是去镇压罢工的。

sentences.en: So another month goes by.
sentences.zh: 于是又过了一个月。

sentences.en: GM continues to feel the pressure until finally, on February 11th, GM essentially gives in.
sentences.zh: 通用汽车继续感受到压力，直到2月11日，通用汽车最终妥协了。

sentences.en: They agree to recognize the union, they effectively make them the sole representative of the workers, and they announce a 10% wage increase.
sentences.zh: 他们同意承认工会，实际上使工会成为工人的唯一代表，并宣布加薪10%。

sentences.en: General Motors workers in Flint get the news of the settlement, and the celebration is spontaneous.
sentences.zh: 弗林特的通用汽车工人得知了和解的消息，庆祝活动自发地开始了。

sentences.en: After the long, patient struggle in the factory, the men go home.
sentences.zh: 在工厂里经历了漫长而耐心的斗争后，工人们回家了。

sentences.en: There was a great sense of release, like the end of a war or the overthrow of a despot.
sentences.zh: 有一种巨大的释放感，就像战争结束或暴君被推翻一样。

sentences.en: Okay, so the workers win and manage to inflict quite a bit of pain on the company.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以工人们赢了，并成功地让公司付出了相当大的代价。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: When all is said and done, they've lost several billion dollars in today's dollars during this strike.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，在这场罢工期间，他们损失了相当于今天价值的数十亿美元。

sentences.en: It's just an enormous cost to the company.
sentences.zh: 这对公司来说是一个巨大的成本。

sentences.en: And what happens is other employers are watching this very carefully, and they are becoming freaked out about what might happen to them.
sentences.zh: 结果是，其他雇主正在非常仔细地观察这一切，他们开始对可能发生在自己身上的事情感到恐慌。

sentences.en: So in March, U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以到了三月，美国

sentences.en: Steel decides that it's going to recognize a union in its industry rather than risk a strike of the kind that we saw at GM.
sentences.zh: 钢铁公司决定承认其行业内的工会，而不是冒着像通用汽车那样罢工的风险。

sentences.en: And pretty soon, union membership is really exploding.
sentences.zh: 很快，工会成员人数呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: We see oil field workers, textile workers, furniture manufacturing workers, food, tobacco, streetcar operators, even newspaper reporters start to unionize.
sentences.zh: 我们看到油田工人、纺织工人、家具制造工人、食品、烟草、电车操作员，甚至报社记者都开始组建工会。

sentences.en: And we go from about 12% of American workers who are unionized in 1935 to about 34% in the early 1950s.
sentences.zh: 工会成员占美国工人的比例从1935年的约12%上升到1950年代初的约34%。

sentences.en: So it really takes off.
sentences.zh: 所以它真的发展起来了。

sentences.en: And all throughout this time, workers who are unionizing are starting to see real gains.
sentences.zh: 在这整个时期，组建工会的工人们开始看到真正的收益。

sentences.en: Their work days are capped at eight hours and their work weeks get capped at 40 hours.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作日被限制在8小时以内，每周工作时间被限制在40小时以内。

sentences.en: They get time and a half pay for overtime if they have to work longer than that.
sentences.zh: 如果必须加班，他们可以获得1.5倍的工资。

sentences.en: Eventually, they start getting healthcare benefits too.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们也开始获得医疗福利。

sentences.en: So this is a huge win for these workers.
sentences.zh: 这对这些工人来说是一个巨大的胜利。

sentences.en: And they really quickly start to see the gains that the companies are reaping being pretty widely distributed.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就开始看到公司获得的收益得到了相当广泛的分配。

sentences.en: So that strike effectively kicked off the modern labor movement.
sentences.zh: 所以那场罢工有效地开启了现代劳工运动。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, it gives us a few really important clues about what might be happening this time.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，它为我们提供了一些非常重要的线索，让我们了解这次可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Noam, what about the 1930s helps us understand what might happen today?
sentences.zh: 那么，诺姆，20世纪30年代的情况如何帮助我们理解今天可能发生的事情？

sentences.en: Well, there are definitely a number of similarities between today and the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，今天和20世纪30年代之间确实有很多相似之处。

sentences.en: Obviously, you have the trauma that workers felt during the pandemic, which is not so different than the trauma that workers felt during the Depression.
sentences.zh: 显然，工人们在疫情期间感受到的创伤，与工人们在大萧条时期感受到的创伤并没有太大区别。

sentences.en: You know, suddenly you feel vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，突然之间你感到脆弱。

sentences.en: You feel betrayed.
sentences.zh: 你感到被背叛。

sentences.en: You feel like these things that you knew to be solid have disappeared.
sentences.zh: 你觉得那些你认为稳固的东西已经消失了。

sentences.en: And you want an institution, maybe something like a union, to give you more security going forward.
sentences.zh: 你想要一个机构，也许像工会这样的组织，为你未来的生活提供更多保障。

sentences.en: The second thing is you have an environment, a political environment, a regulatory environment that's pretty friendly to unions.
sentences.zh: 第二点是，你所处的环境，政治环境、监管环境，对工会非常友好。

sentences.en: Joe Biden, like Franklin
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登，就像20世纪30年代的富兰克林·

sentences.en: Roosevelt in the 1930s, has been incredibly outspoken in support of unions.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福一样，一直非常直言不讳地支持工会。

sentences.en: And some of the federal agencies that work in this area, especially the National Labor Relations Board, have also been incredibly supportive of workers seeking to form unions.
sentences.zh: 在这个领域工作的一些联邦机构，特别是国家劳资关系委员会，也一直非常支持寻求组建工会的工人。

sentences.en: The general counsel of that agency, which enforces workers' labor rights, has been very aggressive in prosecuting things like retaliation
sentences.zh: 该机构的总法律顾问负责执行工人的劳动权利，在起诉诸如报复

sentences.en: against workers who are trying to form unions.
sentences.zh: 试图组建工会的工人等行为方面一直非常积极。

sentences.en: So that also is pretty similar to the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点也和20世纪30年代非常相似。

sentences.en: And then you have to think about where we are in the economy today.
sentences.zh: 然后你必须考虑我们今天在经济中所处的位置。

sentences.en: Just like in the 1930s, we had this traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 就像在20世纪30年代一样，我们经历了一次创伤性事件。

sentences.en: But since then, things have started to get better.
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，情况开始好转。

sentences.en: We now have these labor shortages.
sentences.zh: 我们现在出现了劳动力短缺。

sentences.en: Employers are constantly talking about how they can't get enough workers in the door.
sentences.zh: 雇主们一直在谈论他们如何招不到足够的工人。

sentences.en: But at the same time, the workers feel like they're not sharing in all the gains that the companies are making as the economy bounces back.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，工人们觉得随着经济复苏，他们并没有分享到公司获得的所有收益。

sentences.en: So they feel a kind of disconnect in the way that they did in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 所以他们感到一种脱节，就像他们在20世纪30年代所感受到的那样。

sentences.en: And the last thing is, you have to look at the type of worker who's kind of at the center of this unionization trend.
sentences.zh: 最后一点，你必须看看处于这种工会化趋势中心的工人类型。

sentences.en: If you think back to the 1930s, the people at GM were not the most marginal worker at the lowest rung of the workforce.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想20世纪30年代，通用汽车的工人并不是劳动力中最边缘、处于最底层的工人。

sentences.en: And I think we're seeing something similar today, where the people who are often leading this unionization campaign, many of them
sentences.zh: 我认为我们今天看到了类似的情况，那些经常领导这场工会化运动的人，他们中的许多人

sentences.en: are college-educated people, have graduated from college.
sentences.zh: 都是受过大学教育的人，是从大学毕业的。

sentences.en: That's not to say that people who haven't been to college aren't forming unions too.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说没上过大学的人就没有在组建工会。

sentences.en: But if you look at where these union campaigns appear to be getting traction, it's Starbucks.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看这些工会运动似乎在哪里获得动力，那是星巴克。

sentences.en: It's not McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 不是麦当劳。

sentences.en: It's REI, not Walmart.
sentences.zh: 是REI，不是沃尔玛。

sentences.en: And that's not for lack of effort on the part of unions.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为工会缺乏努力。

sentences.en: Over the past decade or two, we've had some very high-profile unions spend tens of millions of dollars trying to unionize fast food workers, workers at the likes of McDonald's
sentences.zh: 在过去的一二十年里，我们有一些非常引人注目的工会花费了数千万美元试图让快餐业工人、像麦当劳

sentences.en: and Burger King.
sentences.zh: 和汉堡王这样的公司的工人加入工会。

sentences.en: We had a very high-profile campaign that tried to unionize Walmart workers and spent tens of millions of dollars doing that.
sentences.zh: 我们曾进行过一场非常引人注目的运动，试图让沃尔玛工人加入工会，并为此花费了数千万美元。

sentences.en: And those campaigns just never really gained a ton of traction.
sentences.zh: 但这些运动从来没有真正获得太大的动力。

sentences.en: Certainly not the kind of traction that we've seen at Starbucks and REI over the past several months.
sentences.zh: 当然，远没有我们在过去几个月里在星巴克和REI看到的动力那么大。

sentences.en: But Noam, why college grads?
sentences.zh: 但是诺姆，为什么是大学毕业生？

sentences.en: I mean, why are they the special sauce here?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么他们是这里的关键因素？

sentences.en: Well, it really goes back to the Great Recession of 2008.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的要追溯到2008年的大衰退。

sentences.en: That was an incredibly deep and painful recession.
sentences.zh: 那是一场极其深刻且痛苦的衰退。

sentences.en: And what was especially tough about that recession is that people who had recently
sentences.zh: 那场衰退特别艰难的地方在于，那些刚从

sentences.en: graduated from college had an incredibly difficult time finding jobs, at least jobs that were on a par with their skill set.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业的人在找工作时遇到了极大的困难，至少是找不到与他们的技能水平相当的工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember interviewing a bunch of college grads in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我记得2010年左右在华盛顿特区采访了一群大学毕业生。

sentences.en: around 2010.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，两年过去了，他们仍然在卖冰淇淋，而且他们很不开心。

sentences.en: So, of course, two years later, and they were still scooping ice cream and they were pretty unhappy.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在典型的衰退中，这种情况可能会在衰退后持续一两年。

sentences.en: And in a typical recession, that might happen for a year or two after the recession.
sentences.zh: 但我们近年来看到的经济研究表明，这些

sentences.en: But the economics research that we've seen come out in recent years shows that these
sentences.zh: 影响实际上一直持续到大衰退后大约十年左右，一直持续到疫情前夕。

sentences.en: effects actually continued on until about a decade or so after the Great Recession, really right up until the eve of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为从那时起，我们大家都已经认识到了一些非常突出的例子。

sentences.en: And there are some very prominent examples that I think all of us have come to recognize since then.
sentences.zh: 你有亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯众议员，她本人毕业于波士顿大学。
zh_words: 亚历山德里娅·奥卡西奥

sentences.en: You have Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who herself graduated from Boston University.
sentences.zh: 她大学毕业。

sentences.en: She comes out of college.
sentences.zh: 她主修经济学和国际关系，在最终竞选国会议员之前，她的大部分大学毕业后的时光都在做服务员和调酒师。

sentences.en: She majors in economics and international relations and spends much of her post-college years working as a waitress and a bartender before she eventually runs for Congress.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我记得当她出现在公众视野中时，她之所以如此受欢迎，原因之一就是她真正代表了一代人的心声。

sentences.en: I remember when she came onto the scene, one of the reasons she was so popular is because she really spoke to a generation.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And there are a number of people that I've interviewed who are involved in union campaigns now who fit this profile.
sentences.zh: 我采访过不少人，他们现在参与了工会运动，而且都符合这种特征。

sentences.en: I spoke with a man who graduated from Siena College in 2017 with a degree in political science.
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位男士，他于2017年从锡耶纳学院毕业，获得了政治学学位。

sentences.en: He did a number of sort of social service jobs for several years after he graduated, but he never made more than $15 an hour
sentences.zh: 毕业后的几年里，他做过不少社会服务类的工作，但时薪从未超过15美元。

sentences.en: at any of those jobs and finally quit the last one in late 2020.
sentences.zh: 在这些工作中，他最终在2020年底辞去了最后一份。

sentences.en: It took him a while to find another job.
sentences.zh: 他花了一段时间才找到下一份工作。

sentences.en: That job was at Starbucks, where he started at $15.50 an hour as a barista, and that was more than he'd ever made since he graduated from college.
sentences.zh: 那份工作是在星巴克，他起初是一名咖啡师，时薪15.50美元，这比他大学毕业后赚到的任何工资都要高。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I talked to another woman who's a shift supervisor at a Starbucks in Mesa, Arizona.
sentences.zh: 我还采访了另一位女士，她是亚利桑那州梅萨市一家星巴克的轮班主管。

sentences.en: She graduated from Arizona State University with a bachelor's degree in music education.
sentences.zh: 她毕业于亚利桑那州立大学，拥有音乐教育学士学位。

sentences.en: Then she got a master's degree in opera performance.
sentences.zh: 后来她又获得了歌剧表演硕士学位。

sentences.en: She started working at Starbucks not too long after the Great Recession in the early 2010s.
sentences.zh: 她在2010年代初大衰退后不久就开始在星巴克工作了。

sentences.en: And she just ended up staying there after having kids and getting married because she just needed the healthcare.
sentences.zh: 结婚生子后，她最终留在了那里，因为她确实需要医疗保险。

sentences.en: And that was a place where she could get reliable healthcare benefits.
sentences.zh: 那里能为她提供可靠的医疗福利。

sentences.en: So you see a lot of these college-educated folks who, for one reason or another, often having to do with the economy and not having other opportunities,
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到很多受过大学教育的人，由于各种原因——通常与经济状况有关，且缺乏其他机会——

sentences.en: ending up at companies like Starbucks.
sentences.zh: 最终进入了像星巴克这样的公司。

sentences.en: And when they get there, they don't always love it.
sentences.zh: 而当他们进入这些公司后，并不总是感到满意。

sentences.en: They envision themselves maybe doing other things, maybe making more money, maybe having other options.
sentences.zh: 他们设想过自己或许能做点别的，或许能赚更多的钱，或许有其他的选择。

sentences.en: And over the course of 10 or 15 years, this frustration really builds across a whole demographic of workers.
sentences.zh: 在过去10到15年的时间里，这种挫败感在整个劳动者群体中不断积聚。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there's the pandemic, right, which probably makes life a lot harder for the workers you were interviewing.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有疫情，对吧？这可能让你采访的那些工人的生活变得更加艰难了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In a way, I think of what happened after the Great Recession and up until the pandemic as kind of the kindling.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为大衰退之后直到疫情发生前的那段时间，就像是引火物。

sentences.en: You know, this frustration is building and building.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种挫败感在不断累积。

sentences.en: And then you have this pandemic, which really is kind of the spark.
sentences.zh: 然后疫情来了，这真的就像是火星。

sentences.en: People are working in conditions that they think of as unsafe.
sentences.zh: 人们在他们认为不安全的环境中工作。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, their companies are doing very well and oftentimes making record profits.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们的公司却经营得非常好，往往还创下了利润纪录。

sentences.en: And the workers feel like, well, these companies, not only are they not taking care of me and protecting me, but they're not even sharing in
sentences.zh: 工人们觉得，这些公司不仅没有照顾和保护我，甚至连

sentences.en: all of the profits that they're making during this period.
sentences.zh: 他们在这段时期赚取的所有利润都不愿分享。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Noam, based on what you just said, we have a political environment that's friendly towards unions.
sentences.zh: 那么，诺姆，根据你刚才所说的，我们现在有一个对工会友好的政治环境。

sentences.en: We have pent up frustration among workers.
sentences.zh: 工人们心中积压着挫败感。

sentences.en: And we have this type of worker that fuels some agency.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有这种能激发某种能动性的工人。

sentences.en: And companies are doing really well.
sentences.zh: 公司也经营得非常好。

sentences.en: This is sounding a lot like what we saw in the
sentences.zh: 这听起来很像我们在
20世纪30年代看到的情况。

sentences.en: So, does it mean that unions are about to take off?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着工会运动即将兴起？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know, but it's not necessarily a slam dunk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们还不知道，但这未必是板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: And there are two big reasons to keep in mind here.
sentences.zh: 这里有两个重要的原因需要记住。

sentences.en: Number one, workers just have less power today than they did in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 第一，与20世纪30年代相比，今天的工人权力较小。

sentences.en: And that's largely because of the trends in globalization and automation since then.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是因为自那时以来的全球化和自动化趋势。

sentences.en: Today, the typical worker is competing against workers on the other side of the world.
sentences.zh: 今天，典型的工人是在与世界另一端的工人竞争。

sentences.en: They're competing against machines.
sentences.zh: 他们是在与机器竞争。

sentences.en: They're not just competing against the worker down the street.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅仅是在与街对面的工人竞争。

sentences.en: And if you put that together, what that means for employers is that if workers get too expensive or if employers start to think
sentences.zh: 如果你把这些因素综合起来，对雇主而言，这意味着如果工人的成本变得太高，或者雇主开始认为

sentences.en: their workers are getting too pushy, then you can maybe make do with less of them.
sentences.zh: 他们的工人变得太咄咄逼人，那么你或许可以减少用工。

sentences.en: You can replace them with machines.
sentences.zh: 你可以用机器取代他们。

sentences.en: You can send their jobs overseas.
sentences.zh: 你可以把他们的工作外包到海外。

sentences.en: And that just makes workers a lot less powerful.
sentences.zh: 这使得工人的力量大大减弱了。

sentences.en: And the second reason is that companies may be more motivated today to crush unions than they were even back in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，与20世纪30年代相比，今天的公司可能更有动力去打压工会。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, if you think about one other big trend since the
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你想想自

sentences.en: 1930s, it's that we've had a shift from a manufacturing-based economy to a much more service-based economy.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代以来的另一个大趋势，那就是我们的经济已经从制造业为主转向了服务业为主。

sentences.en: And one big consequence of that shift from manufacturing to services is that labor costs typically have a much bigger impact on a company's bottom line.
sentences.zh: 从制造业向服务业转型的一个重大后果是，劳动力成本通常对公司的利润影响更大。

sentences.en: If you think about what service is, it's people.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想什么是服务业，它就是人。

sentences.en: For a company like Starbucks, their labor costs are a big part of their business.
sentences.zh: 对于像星巴克这样的公司来说，劳动力成本是其业务的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Because if you think about all their other inputs, it's milk, it's beans, it's cups.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你想想他们所有的其他投入，比如牛奶、咖啡豆、纸杯。

sentences.en: These things are cheap.
sentences.zh: 这些东西都很便宜。

sentences.en: That's really different than a car plant where labor costs are relatively small because the other inputs are so expensive.
sentences.zh: 这与汽车工厂完全不同，在汽车工厂，劳动力成本相对较小，因为其他投入非常昂贵。

sentences.en: It's glass, it's rubber, steel, big machines.
sentences.zh: 那是玻璃、橡胶、钢材和大型机器。

sentences.en: So when you think about it that way, the person in a service-based company is relatively expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以当你这样想的时候，服务型公司里的员工相对来说是昂贵的。

sentences.en: And what companies like Starbucks have gotten really good at over the past several decades
sentences.zh: 而像星巴克这样的公司在过去几十年里变得非常擅长的一件事

sentences.en: is figuring out how to minimize the cost of that person behind the counter serving you that coffee.
sentences.zh: 就是想方设法将柜台后为你提供咖啡的那位员工的成本降到最低。

sentences.en: They use really sophisticated algorithms and software that tells them at any point in the week or any point in the day how many people they're likely to need.
sentences.zh: 他们使用非常复杂的算法和软件，能告诉他们在每周或每天的任何时候，他们可能需要多少人。

sentences.en: And then they schedule around that.
sentences.zh: 然后他们据此进行排班。

sentences.en: And if it turns out they need even fewer, then they'll send those people home.
sentences.zh: 如果结果发现他们需要的人更少，他们就会让那些人回家。

sentences.en: So you get weird things like shifts that lasted for like three hours and 15 minutes or four hours and 45 minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到一些奇怪的现象，比如轮班时间只有3小时15分钟或4小时45分钟。

sentences.en: This is all because they are trying to minimize their labor costs at any point in time.
sentences.zh: 这都是因为他们试图在任何时候都将劳动力成本降到最低。

sentences.en: I've heard about this.
sentences.zh: 我听说过这个。

sentences.en: This is called just-in-time scheduling.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“即时排班”。

sentences.en: And it can be particularly brutal for workers and very profitable for companies.
sentences.zh: 这对工人来说可能特别残酷，但对公司来说却非常有利可图。

sentences.en: But Noam, what does that have to do with unions and why employers would want to crush them?
sentences.zh: 但是诺姆，这和工会以及雇主为什么要打压工会有什么关系呢？

sentences.en: Well, if you think about what a union does, from a company's perspective, it busts all that apart.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你从公司的角度考虑工会的作用，它会把这一切都打破。

sentences.en: Unions want predictable hours.
sentences.zh: 工会想要可预测的工作时间。

sentences.en: They want more staffing, not less.
sentences.zh: 他们想要增加人手，而不是减少。

sentences.en: They reduce flexibility.
sentences.zh: 他们降低了灵活性。

sentences.en: They increase wages.
sentences.zh: 他们提高了工资。

sentences.en: And because service companies believe that a big part of their game is keeping labor costs low, they may be even more motivated to make sure that unions don't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 由于服务型公司认为保持低劳动力成本是他们获胜的关键，他们可能更有动力确保工会不存在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So before, when manufacturing was king, labor costs were just one small part of what factories were dealing with.
sentences.zh: 所以以前，当制造业称王时，劳动力成本只是工厂所面临的一小部分问题。

sentences.en: Today, we have the service sector and labor costs are a much bigger part of their business.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们有了服务业，劳动力成本在他们的业务中占据了更大的比重。

sentences.en: So if labor costs rise, that goes to the very heart of their business model.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果劳动力成本上升，那将触及他们商业模式的核心。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So Noam, you've told us about this period when unions really took off and how that relates to today.
sentences.zh: 那么诺姆，你告诉了我们工会真正兴起的那段时期，以及它与今天的联系。

sentences.en: But you've also told us that there are some really big obstacles when it comes to unionization right now.
sentences.zh: 但你也告诉我们，目前在工会化方面存在一些非常大的障碍。

sentences.en: And I guess I'm left wondering which force is more powerful in our economy right now?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，在当前的经济中，哪种力量更强大？

sentences.en: I mean, which one is going to win out?
sentences.zh: 我是说，哪一方会胜出？

sentences.en: Well, one thing that we know historically is that growth in union membership tends to come in spurts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们从历史上知道的一件事是，工会成员的增长往往是突发性的。

sentences.en: We get these big waves of growth in union membership that happens in a pretty short amount of time.
sentences.zh: 我们会在很短的时间内看到工会成员人数出现大幅增长。

sentences.en: And I think what that tells you is that once one of these spurts gets going, it can be very hard to stop.
sentences.zh: 我认为这告诉我们，一旦这种增长势头开始，就很难停止。

sentences.en: The momentum just kind of builds on itself.
sentences.zh: 这种势头会自我强化。

sentences.en: Workers at one company see workers at another unionize and they decide they want a union too.
sentences.zh: 一家公司的员工看到另一家公司的员工加入了工会，他们也决定要成立工会。

sentences.en: And now they have evidence that it's possible.
sentences.zh: 现在他们有了证据，证明这是可能的。

sentences.en: And that just kind of keeps going across companies, across industries.
sentences.zh: 这种势头就会在不同公司、不同行业间持续下去。

sentences.en: So I guess the question is, are we at a moment where that has really taken hold?
sentences.zh: 所以我猜问题在于，我们是否正处于这种势头真正形成的时刻？

sentences.en: Are we in a moment where the momentum has built to one of these bona fide spurts?
sentences.zh: 我们是否正处于势头已经积聚到这种真正的爆发增长的时刻？

sentences.en: Or are we still early enough in this process where it hasn't gotten enough momentum?
sentences.zh: 还是说我们仍处于这个过程的早期，势头还不够强？

sentences.en: And employers who don't want this to happen can keep it in check?
sentences.zh: 而那些不希望这种情况发生的雇主还能控制住局面？

sentences.en: I don't really know the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: If you pressed me, I'd say we're not going to see a repeat of what we saw in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 如果非要我回答，我会说我们不会看到20世纪30年代那种情况的重演。

sentences.en: But the thing to keep in mind is that even if we got just a few percentage points increase in the rate of union membership, if we reverse that decades-long
sentences.zh: 但要记住的是，即使工会成员比例只增加了几个百分点，如果我们扭转了那几十年的

sentences.en: decline, that would affect millions of workers directly and probably millions of more workers
sentences.zh: 衰退，那也将直接影响数百万工人，并可能影响更多在类似行业工作的工人，

sentences.en: who work in similar industries and whose employers would probably raise their wages and benefits because they don't want them to unionize.
sentences.zh: 他们的雇主可能会提高工资和福利，因为他们不希望员工加入工会。

sentences.en: So even if we just see a modest upturn, which is entirely possible, the effects on the economy and on American workers could be enormous.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们只看到温和的增长，这也是完全可能的，这对经济和美国工人的影响可能是巨大的。

sentences.en: Noam, thank you.
sentences.zh: 诺姆，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周末，美国众议院议长南希·佩洛西

sentences.en: House of Representatives, made a wartime trip to Kyiv on Saturday and met with Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky.
sentences.zh: 于周六对基辅进行了战时访问，并会见了乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基。

sentences.en: We believe that we are visiting you to say thank you for your fight for freedom.
sentences.zh: 我们相信，我们访问你是为了感谢你们为自由而战。

sentences.en: Ms. Pelosi was the most senior elected American official to visit Kyiv.
sentences.zh: 佩洛西女士是访问基辅的最高级别的美国民选官员。

sentences.en: Her rare frontline trip signals a deepening U.S.
sentences.zh: 她这次罕见的战地之行标志着美国对乌克兰的承诺正在加深，

sentences.en: commitment to Ukraine and comes as some civilians were being evacuated from a steel plant in the embattled Ukrainian port city of Mediupol.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，一些平民正从乌克兰饱受战火蹂躏的港口城市马里乌波尔的一家钢铁厂撤离。

sentences.en: And the European Union will begin an embargo on Russian oil imports at the end of this year,
sentences.zh: 欧盟将在今年年底开始对俄罗斯石油进口实施禁运，

sentences.en: a move that is expected to increase economic pressure on Russia, where oil exports are a major part of the economy.
sentences.zh: 此举预计将增加对俄罗斯的经济压力，因为石油出口是其经济的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: The EU gets, on average, a quarter of its oil every year from Russia, amounting to half of Russia's oil exports.
sentences.zh: 欧盟每年平均从俄罗斯进口四分之一的石油，占俄罗斯石油出口的一半。

sentences.en: Germany was getting more than a third of its oil from Russia at the start of the war, but has, in the past few weeks, cut that to 12 percent.
sentences.zh: 战争开始时，德国从俄罗斯进口的石油超过了其总量的三分之一，但在过去几周里，这一比例已降至12%。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。
